attempts.source:
forall A, B, C set, a A, b B, g fn(x A) fn(y B) C:
    g(a)(b) = g(a)(b)
attempts.evidence: ParseError: name `C` is already active in this scope and cannot be rebound
attempts.lesson: Use fresh user-set names; C is the builtin complex set.

accepted_blocks.source:
forall S, T, U set, a S, b T, g fn(x S) fn(y T) U:
    g(a)(b) = g(a)(b)
accepted_blocks.lesson: The verifier already checks and retains exact unary source application layers.

accepted_blocks.source:
forall S, T, U, V set, a S, b T, c U, g fn(x S) fn(y T) fn(z U) V:
    g(a)(b)(c) = g(a)(b)(c)
accepted_blocks.lesson: The same verifier prefix recipe extends structurally beyond two layers.

accepted_blocks.source:
forall S, T, U set, a S, b T, f fn(x S, y T) U:
    f(a, b) = f(a, b)
accepted_blocks.lesson: A same-layer application retains parameter_index 0 and 1 under one source layer.

accepted_blocks.source:
forall f fn(x, y R: x > 0, y > 0) R:
    forall a, b R:
        a > 0
        b > 0
        =>:
            f(a, b) = f(a, b)
accepted_blocks.lesson: Domain requirements follow the complete parameter telescope and preserve their checked order.

accepted_blocks.source:
have fn first(x, y R) R = x
first(1, 1) = 1
accepted_blocks.lesson: A named function with two parameters uses the same single source-layer telescope and reduces at its checked application.
